Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
Extending from this clarification: www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/79960-nightstick-and-defensive-strikes?start=6#105963

If only ranged strikes, dodge and combat ends are effective at long range, can a minion gain a press by using a "strike:X with optional press" while at long range?

Messages.Author: DavidR
Messages.Body:
normally the strikes will be something like "strike: strength+1, with optional press" so the optional press is not attached to the strike, in long range will hit nothing and still get your press, the "," mekes the diference

Messages.Author: the1andonlime
Messages.Body:
> DavidR wrote:
> normally the strikes will be something like "strike: strength+1, with optional press" so the optional press is not attached to the strike, in long range will hit nothing and still get your press, the "," mekes the diference
>
The rulebook (and clarified in the linked thread) says that non-ranged strikes that are not dodge or combat ends have no effect at long range. You can't get the optional press without using the strike, so it is attached to the strike. Even Nightstick cannot be used to prevent damage at long range, sonit wouldn't be about whether the effect affects the opposing vampire.

I don't see the relevance of a comma here. If that's the difference, Creeping Infection could be argued to have its second effect work at long range.

Meat Hook has explicit text but it makes sense from a "lore" perspective even without the text. Lam Into giving the press at long range makes no sense from a "lore" perspective, which is what initially made me ask the question.

Messages.Author: KoRneeshon
Messages.Body:
The optional press is not attached to the strike, like DavidR said. Read it logically as:
(strike:X) + (optional press)

rather than:
(strike:x with optional press)

The optional press gain is effect of the card, not the effect of the strike.

Messages.Author: Palamedes
Messages.Body:
With an example:

1. Can a minion play Lam Into (vic, hand strike) if the round is set at long range (without dealing damage of course)?
2. If yes, does the minion get an optional press?
3. If yes, does the new round is set at close range?

Lam Into

Warning: Spoiler!

Cardtype: Combat
Requires an Anarch. Do not replace until after combat. Strike: hand strike or use a melee weapon strike.
[for] This strike is at +1 damage, with 1 optional maneuver.
[pot] This strike is at +2 damage.
[vic] This strike is at +1 damage, with 1 optional press. If another round of combat occurs, that round is at close range (skip the determine range step for that round).

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> the1andonlime wrote:
> Extending from this clarification: www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/79960-nightstick-and-defensive-strikes?start=6#105963
>
> If only ranged strikes, dodge and combat ends are effective at long range, can a minion gain a press by using a "strike:X with optional press" while at long range?
>
No, since the strike is not effective, and the press is tied to the strike.

REVERSAL: The strike has no effect on the opposing minion, but you still have a press.
see www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/83009-clarification-effective-strike#117087

Prince of Paris, France

> Q: If I use Blood of the Cobra and play Dagon's Call as my strike at long
> range, is it still a hand strike?
> A: No. Dagon's call becomes "Strike: ranged. Make a hand strike ... and the
> opposing minion takes 1 unpreventable damage during the press step..."
> The modified Dagon's Call strike is not a hand strike, and the hand strike
> made as part of its effect is not effective at long range, although the
> rest of the Dagon's Call effect is.
>
> Q: If I use Blood of the Cobra and play Scorpion's Touch as my strike and use
> it with my Bastard Sword, what effect does it have?
> A: Similar to above. Scorpion's Touch makes your Bastard Sword strike a
> "Strike: Make a bastard sword strike and put this card on the opposing
> minion..." and Blood of the Cobra makes that a "Strike: ranged. Make a
> bastard sword strike and put this card on the opposing minion..." The
> Bastard Sword strike does no damage at long range, but the rest of the
> effect ("put this card on the opposing minion...") is applied.
>
If we are using whether or not the strike is effective to determine then would this not be reversal for that as nothing in Blood of the Cobra has said or says apply parts of the strike as it has relied on it just being ranged strike so the effects would apply even for uneffective strikes. Now with things being tied to strike being effective it seems they no longer do?

[QUI] As above, and this hand strike is at +1 damage. Artist: Durwin Talon

As placing cards on the opposing minion is not mentioned in the clarification  www.vekn.net/forum/rules-questions/83009-clarification-effective-strike#117087 and there is existing ruling on it, I'm assuming the ruling on Blood of the Cobra and Scorpion's touch still applies, the damage is not effective but the card is placed on the opposing minion.

If it is not I appreciate if placing cards is added to the list as it is reversal to the LSJ ruling that allows it.

Or allowing that ruling stand for now until a change to the cardtext on Blood of the Cobra is made to prevent that. Potential future uses in other cards allowing such shenigans naturally will follow whatever the POD text is deemed to be.
